# Brief: "Gripper Rush", a single-file HTML game

Write a complete browser game as one self-contained HTML file (inline CSS and JavaScript, no external
libraries, fonts, images or URLs, no build step). It must work by double-clicking the file.

**Theme.** The player operates an overhead robot gripper (like a claw machine / pick-and-place arm)
above a conveyor belt. Objects of different shapes slide along the belt from left to right. Each round
a target shape is shown ("pick: CUBES"). The player moves the gripper left/right, lowers it, and
closes it to grasp, then carries the object to the bin on the right and drops it.

**Goal and rules.**
- Score points for every correct object dropped in the bin (+10). Wrong object in the bin: -5 and lose a life.
- Objects that pass the end of the belt are simply lost (no penalty), except target objects: missing a
  target costs one life.
- 3 lives. The game ends when lives reach 0 (lose) or when the score reaches 150 (win).
- The belt gets faster as the score rises. The target shape changes every 5 correct picks.
- A grasp only succeeds if the gripper is lowered while centred over the object (within a tolerance);
  a missed grasp wastes time (the gripper must rise again).

**Controls.** Arrow Left/Right (or A/D) move the gripper; Space lowers + grasps if empty, or lowers +
releases if holding (release over the bin = drop in bin; elsewhere = object falls back onto the belt).
Also support on-screen buttons for touch/mouse (Left, Right, Grab/Drop). P pauses.

**Screens.** Start screen with title, the rules in 3-4 short lines and a "Start" button (Enter also
starts). HUD with score, lives, current target, speed level. Game-over screen that clearly says
"You win" or "Game over", the final score, the best score this session, and a "Restart" button
(R also restarts). Restart must fully reset state.

**Quality.** Use <canvas> with requestAnimationFrame and delta-time movement; draw the gripper,
belt, bin and shapes (cube, sphere, cylinder drawn as square, circle, rounded rectangle) with
distinct colours. Keep the code readable with short comments. No console errors.




Return the complete game as ONE ```html code block (a full document starting with <!DOCTYPE html>). No other files, no external URLs.
